rule.title: Visa Fraud Monitoring Program
rule.note: This reason code generally cannot be represented. Recommend accepting liability unless the merchant can prove the transaction was miscoded by the issuer.

summary.allegation: The issuer has raised the transaction under the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program, asserting that this GBP 78.50 payment of 30 April 2025 forms part of a merchant fraud-monitoring case rather than a standard disputed sale.
summary.to_defend: Under Visa 10.5 the only defence is proof that the issuer miscoded the transaction under the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program; evidence about the merits of the sale does not qualify.

requirements.title: Proof the issuer miscoded the chargeback
requirements.text: Evidence that the transaction was miscoded by the issuer under the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program.
requirements.finding: Nothing supplied addresses miscoding by the issuer. The merchant has filed a Visa Secure authentication record and a delivery confirmation, which speak to the legitimacy of the sale, not to whether the issuer wrongly coded it under the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program.
requirements.gap: No evidence that the transaction was reported or coded in error under the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program, for example issuer or Visa correspondence confirming the case was raised against the wrong transaction or merchant identifier.

documents.label: Visa Secure authentication record
documents.reason: Shows 3DS authentication for txn_1178ST but goes to the merits of the sale, not to issuer miscoding under the Fraud Monitoring Program, which is the only exception for 10.5.

documents.label: Carrier delivery confirmation, order BB-77231
documents.reason: Confirms delivery of the goods; delivery merits do not meet the miscoding exception required to represent a 10.5 chargeback.

alerts.text: Visa 10.5 generally cannot be represented. The evidence is shown but does not change the outcome unless it proves miscoding.

justification: Accept liability: R1, the sole defence for Visa 10.5, requires proof of issuer miscoding, and no such evidence exists in the file.
rationale:
The issuer has processed this GBP 78.50 transaction of 30 April 2025 under Visa reason code 10.5, Visa Fraud Monitoring Program.
Reason code 10.5 cannot be represented except on proof that the issuer miscoded the transaction under the programme, and no such proof has been supplied.
The two documents filed, the Visa Secure record for txn_1178ST and the Evri delivery confirmation for order BB-77231 delivered 2 May 2025, address the merits of the sale only.
Strong authentication data (3DS authenticated, AVS Y, CVV M) does not create a defence under this code.
Recommend accepting liability and, separately, reviewing the merchant's fraud ratios with Visa outside the chargeback process.
